payload.problem_addressed: Inference-time scaling for diffusion/flow-matching models is far less developed than for autoregressive LMs, and final quality is highly sensitive to the initial noise seed.
payload.method_summary: Progressive Seed Pruning (PSP) scores intermediate denoised estimates and progressively narrows the candidate seed set so only promising trajectories are fully denoised, front-loading exploration across many seeds early while keeping total model evaluations fixed.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper introduces Progressive Seed Pruning (PSP), an inference-time scaling method for diffusion and flow-matching models that evaluates many noise seeds early and progressively narrows the candidate set based on intermediate denoised estimates, using a fixed compute budget more effectively than existing best-of-N or resampling approaches. Across diffusion and flow-matching backbones, PSP improves reward-guided selection and achieves higher automated (GenEval) and human-evaluated prompt-alignment scores than best-of-N, importance-sampling, and tree-search baselines at matched compute.
key_architecture_choices: Scores intermediate denoised estimates rather than only final outputs
Progressively narrows the candidate pool (tree-search-like pruning) instead of a constant memory footprint
payload.headline_results: PSP consistently improves reward-guided selection and achieves higher GenEval scores and better human evaluation on prompt-alignment than best-of-N, importance-sampling, and tree-search baselines at matched compute.
claimed_advantages: Uses a fixed compute budget more effectively than best-of-N/importance-sampling/tree-search
Front-loads exploration across seeds early rather than maintaining a constant memory footprint
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: The progressive-pruning-under-fixed-budget mechanism is transferable to our best-of-N program screening against the frozen verifier: score partial/intermediate decoder rollouts and prune low-promise candidates early instead of fully executing/verifying every candidate to completion, evaluating more candidates within the same verifier-call budget.
payload.reviewer_notes: Domain is image diffusion/flow-matching, not autoregressive program synthesis, so the scoring signal (denoised-estimate quality) would need to be replaced by a partial-program value estimate or fast proxy verifier; the core budget-allocation idea (front-load exploration, prune progressively) is architecture-agnostic.

provenance.problem_addressed: inference-time scaling for these models is far less developed than for autoregressive language models
provenance.method_summary: Progressive Seed Pruning (\PSP) scores intermediate denoised estimates and progressively narrows the candidate set
provenance.contributions_summary: achieves higher GenEval scores (automated) and better human evaluation on prompt-alignment
provenance.headline_results: achieves higher GenEval scores (automated) and better human evaluation on prompt-alignment than best-of-$N$, importance-sampling, and tree-search baselines at matched compute
provenance.claimed_advantages: we can use a fixed compute budget more effectively

payload.problem_addressed: Best-of-N (BoN) selection assumes complete candidates can be reliably evaluated, but many vision-language tasks only provide partial verification of findings/spans/values/regions/relations, with no dependable whole-response verifier.
payload.method_summary: Best-of-Evidence (BoE) keeps the BoN candidate pool fixed, represents reusable claims via a signed candidate-factor graph, and allocates a limited evidence budget to evidence actions that can change the final selection via a practical score-based controller; the zero-budget case recovers plain BoN.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper introduces Best-of-Evidence (BoE), an inference-time selection framework for best-of-N candidate pools under partial verification, using a signed candidate-factor claim graph and a budget-limited evidence controller. It provides theoretical results showing residual evidence capacity bounds achievable improvement and that shared factor queries can achieve O(log K) versus Theta(K) query cost separation, and shows empirically on four medical VQA settings that BoE can improve fixed-pool selection and rescue some BoN failures.
key_architecture_choices: Signed candidate-factor graph representing reusable claims across candidates
Score-based controller allocating a limited evidence-action budget
Zero-budget case reduces exactly to standard BoN
payload.headline_results: Common-ledger experiments on four medical VQA settings show that BoE can improve fixed-pool selection and rescue some BoN failures when evidence is reliable, contrastive, and decision-relevant.
claimed_advantages: Zero-budget case recovers the underlying BoN decision
Shared factor queries achieve O(log K) vs Theta(K) query separation
limitations: Reveals channel-quality and candidate-generation limits that prevent universal gains
Residual evidence capacity limits any evidence-driven improvement
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: Our verifier is a frozen set of independent partial checks (compiles, zero inverted elements, Jacobian/aspect-ratio bounds, surface-match fidelity, feature-edge capture, element-budget) rather than one whole-program verifier -- BoE's idea of representing these partial checks as a shared claim/factor graph across the N candidate programs and adaptively allocating verifier-check budget to the checks most likely to change which candidate is selected could reduce the number of full verifier runs needed during best-of-N screening.
payload.reviewer_notes: Application domain is medical VQA, quite far from CAD/mesh program generation, and the theoretical guarantees are stated for a 'factor-code model' abstraction whose fit to our verifier's check structure is unproven; would need validation that our verifier checks are similarly decomposable and reusable across candidates.

provenance.problem_addressed: Many vision-language tasks instead provide only partial verification: a finding, span, value, region, or relation may be checkable even when no dependable whole-response verifier exists.
provenance.method_summary: keeps the BoN candidate pool fixed, represents reusable claims with a signed candidate--factor graph, and allocates a limited budget to evidence actions
provenance.contributions_summary: shared factor queries can achieve an O(log K) versus Θ(K) query separation in a factor-code model
provenance.headline_results: Common-ledger experiments on four medical VQA settings show that BoE can improve fixed-pool selection and rescue some BoN failures
provenance.limitations: revealing the channel-quality and candidate-generation limits that prevent universal gains

payload.problem_addressed: Existing RLVR approaches for optimized code generation rely on outcome-based signals (correctness, speedup) and overlook performance-critical structural properties of programs essential to generating optimized code.
payload.method_summary: CudaPerf is a reflective RL framework combining verifiable execution rewards with structural code-aware rewards derived from parallelization features (memory coalescing, occupancy, arithmetic intensity, synchronization patterns), operating in two stages: an offline pairwise contrastive ranking module to distinguish strong/weak candidates, then an online RL phase jointly optimizing correctness, performance, and structural efficiency via a unified reward, plus iterative refinement using execution feedback.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper proposes CudaPerf, a reflective reinforcement-learning framework for CUDA kernel generation that augments verifiable execution rewards with structural, parallelization-aware code rewards, trained in an offline contrastive-ranking stage followed by online RL with iterative execution-feedback refinement. It also introduces a dataset of 2.9k C-to-CUDA and 1k PyTorch-to-CUDA programs with diverse implementations and input configurations, and shows CudaPerf substantially outperforms strong baselines (Qwen-3-32B, CUDA Agent) in both speedup and correctness.
key_architecture_choices: Offline pairwise ranking module for contrastive comparison of program candidates
Online RL phase with a unified reward combining correctness, performance, and structural efficiency
Iterative refinement loop using execution feedback
Structural code-aware rewards from parallelization features (memory coalescing, occupancy, Arithmetic Intensity, synchronization patterns)
datasets: 2.9k C-to-CUDA and 1k PyTorch-to-CUDA programs with diverse input configurations and multiple CUDA implementations
payload.headline_results: CudaPerf outperforms Qwen-3-32B (C to CUDA) and CUDA Agent (PyTorch to CUDA) by up to 5x and 3.32x improvements in speedup, and 17% and 7% improvements in correctness, respectively.
claimed_advantages: Combines verifiable execution rewards with structural code-aware rewards, not just outcome-based signals
Iterative refinement via execution feedback enables progressive improvement of generated candidates
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: The two-stage recipe -- offline contrastive pairwise ranking of program candidates followed by online RL with a unified reward combining execution/structural-validity signals, plus iterative execution-feedback refinement of the model's own broken rollouts -- maps closely onto our best-of-N plus frozen-verifier setup: our verifier's compile/valid-mesh/quality-bound checks could serve as the structural and execution reward terms for an analogous RL or DAgger-style repair-distillation loop on hexgen's own rollouts.
payload.reviewer_notes: Domain is CUDA kernel code generation rather than CAD/mesh DSL programs, but both are settings where autoregressive decoders must emit programs that both execute correctly and satisfy secondary structural-quality properties beyond bare validity -- the reward-decomposition approach (execution correctness + structural/quality-aware terms) is a close conceptual match to our verifier's multi-criteria checks (Jacobian/aspect-ratio quality, feature-edge capture, element-budget sanity).

provenance.problem_addressed: existing RLVR approaches primarily rely on outcome-based signals such as correctness and speedup, overlooking performance-critical structural properties of programs
provenance.method_summary: CudaPerf, a reflective RL framework that incorporates both verifiable execution rewards and structural code-aware rewards derived from parallelization features
provenance.contributions_summary: We also introduce a dataset comprising 2.9k C to CUDA and 1k PyTorch to CUDA programs
provenance.headline_results: achieving up to 5X & 3.32X improvements in speedup, and 17% & 7% improvements in correctness, respectively
provenance.claimed_advantages: CudaPerf utilizes iterative refinement using execution feedback enabling progressive improvement of generated candidates

payload.impact_rationale: Would mainly buy compute efficiency in best-of-N screening (more candidates evaluated per verifier-call budget), not a direct increase in structural-validity rate.
payload.effort_rationale: Requires designing a partial-program value/scoring signal analogous to 'intermediate denoised estimate quality' for our discrete program decoder, a nontrivial but bounded engineering task.

payload.impact_rationale: Could reduce redundant full verifier runs during best-of-N screening if our multi-criteria checks decompose like their factor graph, but this is unproven for our verifier and the paper's own results show gains are not universal.
payload.effort_rationale: Building a signed candidate-factor claim graph plus a budget-aware evidence controller around our verifier's checks is a substantial new subsystem, and the medical-VQA setting is far from our domain.

payload.impact_rationale: The reward decomposition (execution correctness + structural/quality-aware terms) closely mirrors our verifier's multi-criteria checks, and could directly power a DAgger-style repair-distillation or RL loop that raises structural validity.
payload.effort_rationale: Requires an offline contrastive ranking stage plus an online RL training phase with a unified reward, on top of our existing supervised-imitation pipeline -- a sizable but well-scoped project.
